prompts.L1:

Provided is a pneumatic tire including a tread portion, sidewall portions, and bead portions. The tread portion comprises a center main groove extending in the tire circumferential direction and a shoulder main groove located outward of the center main groove and extending in the tire circumferential direction. A land portion is defined between the center main groove and the shoulder main groove. The center main groove has a zigzag shape in the tire circumferential direction. Lug grooves extending inward from the shoulder main groove in the tire lateral direction and terminating without communicating with the center main groove are provided in the land portion. A bent portion bent toward a first side in the tire circumferential direction is formed at a terminating end of each of the lug grooves. Narrow grooves extending discontinuously in the tire circumferential direction without communicating with the bent portions are formed in the land portion.

outputs.L1: Provided is a pneumatic tire comprising a tread portion, sidewall portions, and bead portions. The tread portion includes a center main groove extending in the tire circumferential direction and a shoulder main groove positioned outward of the center main groove and extending in the tire circumferential direction. A land portion is defined between the center main groove and the shoulder main groove. The center main groove has a zigzag configuration extending in the tire circumferential direction. The land portion is provided with lug grooves that extend inward from the shoulder main groove in the tire lateral direction and terminate without communicating with the center main groove. A bent portion extending toward a first side in the tire circumferential direction is formed at a terminating end of each lug groove. The land portion is further provided with narrow grooves that extend discontinuously in the tire circumferential direction without communicating with the bent portions.
outputs.L2: A pneumatic tire is disclosed with a tread region, a pair of sidewall regions, and bead regions. The tread region includes a central main groove and a shoulder-side main groove, both running circumferentially around the tire, with the shoulder-side groove positioned laterally outside the central groove. These grooves delimit an intervening land region. The central main groove follows a circumferential zigzag path. Within the land region, lug grooves extend laterally inward from the shoulder-side main groove but end before reaching the central main groove. The terminal end of each lug groove includes a bend directed toward a first circumferential side. The land region further contains narrow grooves arranged intermittently along the tire circumference and isolated from the bent ends of the lug grooves.
outputs.L3:
The pneumatic tire includes a tread portion, a pair of sidewall portions extending from the tread portion, and bead portions provided at the respective inner ends of the sidewall portions. The tread portion is provided with a center main groove extending continuously in the tire circumferential direction and a shoulder main groove positioned outward of the center main groove in the tire lateral direction.

A land portion is defined between the center main groove and the shoulder main groove. The center main groove has a zigzag configuration along the tire circumferential direction. A plurality of lug grooves extend laterally inward from the shoulder main groove into the land portion. Each lug groove terminates within the land portion without communicating with the center main groove, and its terminating end is bent toward a first side in the tire circumferential direction.

A plurality of narrow grooves is also formed within the land portion. These narrow grooves are arranged discontinuously in the tire circumferential direction and are separated from the bent portions of the lug grooves, such that the narrow grooves do not communicate with the bent portions.
outputs.L4:
A pneumatic tire includes a tread portion provided with a zigzag circumferential groove near the center of the tread and a circumferential shoulder groove positioned outwardly in the tire-width direction. A land portion is defined between these grooves. Within the land portion, a plurality of lug grooves are arranged at intervals in the tire-circumferential direction. Each lug groove extends inwardly from the shoulder groove toward the center of the tread and includes a bent terminal portion that ends within the land portion without communicating with the center groove.

The land portion also contains a plurality of narrow grooves formed separately from the lug grooves. These narrow grooves are discontinuous and terminate within the land portion, so they do not establish direct communication between the center groove, the shoulder groove, and the lug grooves. The bent ends of the lug grooves and the independently arranged narrow grooves increase the number of effective edge components that engage the road surface. This improves traction, particularly on wet, snowy, or otherwise low-friction surfaces.

At the same time, the absence of continuous transverse grooves prevents the land portion from being divided into excessively small or flexible blocks. The resulting noncommunicating groove arrangement therefore maintains sufficient tread rigidity, helping to preserve steering stability, cornering performance, and resistance to irregular wear. The center and shoulder grooves provide primary drainage paths, while the lug grooves and narrow grooves collect and guide water toward those paths. By balancing drainage and edge effectiveness with land rigidity, the tread configuration supports improved traction, wet-weather performance, handling stability, and durability.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a pneumatic tire with zigzag center and shoulder main grooves, blind lug grooves having bent terminal ends, and discontinuous narrow circumferential grooves.
counterfactuals.output: A pneumatic tire includes a tread portion having a plurality of circumferentially extending main grooves defining center land portions and shoulder land portions. At least one center main groove and at least one shoulder main groove extend in a zigzag configuration in a tire circumferential direction. The land portions are provided with a plurality of lug grooves extending in a tire axial direction, at least some of the lug grooves being blind grooves that terminate within a respective land portion. Each blind lug groove includes a terminal end bent relative to a principal extending direction of the blind lug groove. One or more narrow circumferential grooves are formed in at least one of the land portions and comprise groove segments arranged discontinuously in the tire circumferential direction. The zigzag main grooves, bent terminal ends, and discontinuous narrow circumferential grooves cooperate to provide drainage and traction while maintaining tread rigidity, steering stability, and resistance to uneven wear.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical description of a tire tread design featuring a land portion between a center main groove and a shoulder main groove, ensuring the lug grooves do not communicate with the center groove.
counterfactuals.output: A tire tread includes a land portion defined between a center main groove and a shoulder main groove, both extending circumferentially. Multiple lug grooves extend from the shoulder main groove into the land portion and terminate within the land portion, thereby remaining isolated from and not communicating with the center main groove.

counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for a pneumatic tire comprising tread, sidewall, and bead portions, with discontinuous narrow grooves formed in a land portion and isolated from bent portions of terminating lug grooves.
counterfactuals.output:
A pneumatic tire includes a tread portion, a pair of sidewall portions extending radially inward from the tread edges, and bead portions located at the radially inner ends of the sidewall portions. The tread portion has one or more land portions defined by circumferential and/or lateral grooves. Lug grooves extend into at least one land portion and terminate therein, each terminating end having a bent portion.

A plurality of narrow grooves is formed discontinuously in the land portion. Each narrow groove is spaced from, and does not communicate with, the bent portion of any terminating lug groove, so that rubber remains between them. This isolated arrangement maintains land rigidity and limits stress concentration or crack propagation while allowing local tread deformation, thereby improving traction, wear resistance, and durability.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the structural features of a tire tread pattern in formal patent language, including the locations, directions, shapes, and communication relationships of its center groove, shoulder groove, lug grooves, and narrow grooves.
counterfactuals.output: A tire tread pattern comprises a center groove extending continuously in a tire circumferential direction within a tread-center region and a pair of shoulder grooves disposed on opposite sides of the center groove in a tire-width direction, each shoulder groove extending generally in the circumferential direction. A plurality of lug grooves are arranged at intervals in the circumferential direction and extend obliquely or generally laterally outward from the center groove toward respective tread edges, each lug groove communicating at an inner end with the center groove and at an intermediate portion with a corresponding shoulder groove. The center groove, shoulder grooves, and lug grooves define a plurality of center blocks and shoulder blocks, the grooves having straight, curved, bent, or zigzag configurations as viewed in plan. Narrow grooves, having a width smaller than that of the lug grooves, are formed in selected center and/or shoulder blocks and extend in a lateral or oblique direction. Each narrow groove communicates at one end with the center groove, a shoulder groove, or a lug groove, while an opposite end terminates within the associated block or communicates with another adjacent groove, thereby establishing predetermined fluid-discharge paths across the tread surface.
